chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was seated, saying: 'I have been given from the zakat, so may I gather it until I perform Hajj with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. May Allah reward the one who gives you.'
ai.seo_question: Can I save my zakat money to perform Hajj later?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the permissibility of accumulating zakat funds for a specific, significant purpose like Hajj, illustrating the flexibility of zakat as disposable wealth once received. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the recipient gains full ownership (malikiyyah) of the zakat, allowing them to prioritize long-term religious obligations over immediate distribution. The Imam’s phrase 'Allah will reward the one who gives you' highlights the dual spiritual benefit for both the giver and the recipient who utilizes the wealth for worship.
